Detector `owner` assignment in `src/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/validators/base/detector.py` (update at :65-77, create at :119-127) has no organization-membership validation — neither update() nor create() checks that the resolved user/team belongs to the detector's organization, relying entirely on ActorField to scope the lookup; if ActorField resolves actors globally by ID, any org member could set an arbitrary user/team ID as owner, creating a cross-org actor reference (IDOR-adjacent).

Unauthenticated browser reporting collector endpoint (`src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py`) logs raw attacker-controlled payloads — the new `browser_report_validation_failed` warning writes the complete raw report and validation errors for every request, letting unauthenticated callers flood the log pipeline with arbitrary content (log-storage cost/DoS) and land CSP-violation bodies (URLs, referrers, query-string tokens) in logs unfiltered.

Analytics event `preprod_artifact.api.assemble` in `src/sentry/preprod/api/endpoints/organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py:80-87` is recorded before the `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble")` gate and before any payload validation, so every rejected request (feature disabled, bad payload) still emits the event — the analytics signal can't distinguish real assembles from rejected/spam requests and any authenticated org member can generate unbounded events.

Timestamp unit mismatch in `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`: error-event timestamps from nodestore are seconds since epoch (~1.7e9) while RRWeb segment/breadcrumb events carry millisecond timestamps (~1.7e12), so the interleaving comparison always emits all error messages before all breadcrumb messages, defeating the chronological merge and degrading the Seer summary it feeds.
In the same breadcrumb/error merge comparison, a non-numeric breadcrumb `timestamp` value would raise a TypeError from the `<` comparison, causing a 500 error.

Possible AttributeError breaking merged-PR comment rendering: `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` in `src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py:~598-604` calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(...)`, but the diff defines `_truncate_title` on `CommitContextIntegration`, and callers in `src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:406` and `src/sentry/integrations/gitlab/integration.py:254` invoke `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)`/`self.get_environment_info(...)` from inside `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow`/`GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body` where `self` is the workflow (holding the integration by composition), not the integration — unless the truncated diff adds these methods to PRCommentWorkflow, both references fail with AttributeError and break merged-PR comment posting for GitHub and GitLab entirely.

Unbounded nodestore materialization: fetch_error_details in project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py takes error_ids verbatim from the replay record with no cap and bulk-fetches the full event payload for every error via nodestore.backend.get_multi, potentially materializing multi-MB of event data per request with no limit, slicing, or projection, scaling cost as pages × total_errors

Redundant per-page backend fetching: query_replay_instance (Snuba), process_raw_response, and nodestore.get_multi all run on every paginated request even though the error context is identical for every page of the same replay

gen_request_data resets error_idx = 0 per invocation and unconditionally yields all remaining error events at the tail, so every page's Seer prompt contains all of the replay's error messages plus that page's breadcrumbs — O(pages × total_errors) payload and token cost, with per-page summaries polluted by out-of-window errors

N+1 recommended-event fetches in PR comment construction: get_environment_info in commit_context.py calls issue.get_recommended_event() (one Snuba latest-event query plus a nodestore fetch) per issue inside the get_comment_body list comprehension, when the issues could be resolved in a bulk eventstore lookup

Wasted Snuba query when error context is disabled: query_replay_instance and process_raw_response execute before the enable_error_context=false check in project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py, so the query result is never used on that path; the disable_error_fetching branch should short-circuit before the query

Fragile positional pairing of event IDs to nodestore results: zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes get_multi's values() preserves input order with no missing-node handling, so error_ids[i] can be paired with the wrong event's data — a latent correctness bug if ErrorEvent["id"] is ever used downstream; should map node_id → event_id and look up by key

New PR-comment helper methods (`_truncate_title`, `get_environment_info`, `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template`) are defined on `CommitContextIntegration` in `src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py`, but all call sites (`GitHubPRCommentWorkflow`, `GitlabPRCommentWorkflow`, `PRCommentWorkflow`) invoke them through workflow objects that do not inherit from the integration ABC, so every merged-PR suspect-comment build for GitHub and GitLab will raise `AttributeError`, silently breaking the PR-bot comment feature; `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title` is also a fragile cross-class reference that should use `self`/`cls`.

In `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, the comparison `error_events[error_idx]['timestamp'] < event.get('timestamp', 0)` compares an ISO-8601 string timestamp from nodestore error events against a numeric epoch-millisecond RRWeb event timestamp, raising an unhandled `TypeError` and 500-ing the summarize-breadcrumbs endpoint whenever a replay has error events; even if the type were coerced, the seconds-vs-milliseconds unit mismatch would misorder errors relative to breadcrumbs, corrupting the AI summary input.

`zip(error_ids, events.values())` in `fetch_error_details` mispairs error IDs with events whenever any error event is missing from nodestore (since `get_multi` omits missing node ids), attributing the wrong title/message to the wrong error and dropping the remaining errors; it should iterate `error_ids` and look up each `node_id` in the returned dict instead of relying on positional alignment.

The new `ChoiceField` validation on `type` in `src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py` 422s previously-accepted report types, but the Reporting API's type set is extensible (legacy `feature-policy-violation`, `ReportingObserver.generateReport` custom types, future spec types), so valid browser telemetry is silently dropped since 422s are effectively non-retriable at this externally consumed boundary.

The fail-fast validation loop in the browser reporting collector rejects the entire POST batch on the first invalid report, discarding valid reports alongside invalid ones; it should skip-and-log invalid entries rather than failing the whole batch.

`if self.initial_data.get('age')` in `validate_timestamp`/`validate_age` treats `age: 0` as absent (symmetrically `timestamp: 0`), so a report carrying both `age: 0` and `timestamp` passes validation, violating the spec's exactly-one rule; it should use `'age' in self.initial_data`.

The exported symbol `ParameterizationRegexExperiment` is deleted from `src/sentry/grouping/parameterization.py` with no deprecation path, so any external importer (getsentry, tooling) now gets an `ImportError`.

The automator-modifiable option `grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent` is unregistered from `src/sentry/options/defaults.py` with no deprecation path, leaving any environment that stored a value with an orphaned option that options tooling will reject on read/write.

`analytics.record('preprod_artifact.api.assemble', ...)` in `src/sentry/preprod/api/endpoints/organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py` fires before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check, so requests subsequently denied (403) are counted as assembles, giving downstream consumers inflated/misleading counts; the record should be moved after the gate and validation, or the event renamed to reflect 'attempted'.

Error-context extraction in `project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py` reads `error_ids` via `process_raw_response(snuba_response, fields=request.query_params.getlist('field'))`; if `process_raw_response` projects strictly onto the supplied fields, callers that don't send `field=error_ids` — including existing clients during deploy skew — silently get zero error context, making the feature a no-op.

`src/sentry/snuba/ourlogs.py:167` now always passes `equations=equations` to `rpc_dataset_common.run_top_events_timeseries_query`; if that callee's signature was not updated (possibly in the truncated portion of the diff), every logs top-events timeseries call raises a `TypeError`.

PR-comment helper methods (`_truncate_title`, `get_environment_info`, `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template`) are defined on `CommitContextIntegration` but invoked on `PRCommentWorkflow` subclass instances in `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body` / `GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body`; since `OpenPRCommentWorkflow` composes rather than inherits `CommitContextIntegration`, every merged-PR comment with ≥1 linked issue raises `AttributeError`, breaking the GitHub/GitLab PR-bot comment feature (src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py:~577-607)

Unguarded, unconditional Snuba call in the summarize-breadcrumbs request path (src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:~66-91): `query_replay_instance` + `process_raw_response` run with no try/except and execute even when `enable_error_context=false`, so a transient Snuba error/timeout 500s the entire endpoint instead of degrading to a breadcrumbs-only summary, and wastes a Snuba query per request when error context is disabled

`fetch_error_details` zips `error_ids` with `nodestore.get_multi` values (`zip(error_ids, events.values())` in project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:~103-107); since nodestore `get_multi` omits missing keys, any missing (retention-expired/purged) event silently shifts the pairing and misattributes error data (wrong title/message/timestamp), which is then swallowed by the broad `except Exception` — should use key-based lookup (`events.get(node_id)`) instead

`error_ids` extraction in project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:~77-83 depends on the client's `field` query params: `process_raw_response(snuba_response, fields=request.query_params.getlist("field"))` means if the caller doesn't include `error_ids` in its field list, the key is absent and error context silently vanishes with no error or metric; the internally needed fields should be requested explicitly (e.g., union `["error_ids"]` into the field list)

Browser reporting collector validation loop (src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:~104-116) returns 422 on the first invalid report, discarding all valid reports in the same batch; since browsers resend the whole batch on failure, a single permanently-malformed report poisons its batch-mates until the attempts cap is hit

Browser reporting collector validators (`validate_timestamp`/`validate_age`) do not enforce presence of `age` or `timestamp`: a report with neither field passes validation, contradicting the stated spec where both Working and Editor's drafts require one of the two fields

Misleading method name: `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` returns a rendered string, not a template

`zip(error_ids, events.values())` in `fetch_error_details` (src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:~109-125) mispairs error IDs with event data because `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a node_id-keyed mapping with no ordering guarantee and omits missing keys entirely; the `if data is not None` guard only helps on backends that return None for misses, making the code backend-dependent — should build a node_id to event_id map and iterate `events.items()`

Broad `except Exception: capture_exception(e); return []` in `fetch_error_details` (project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:~121-124) swallows everything including programming errors and silently produces a summary with no error context; the exception should be narrowed or logged at warning with context

Endpoint's core input depends on the client's `field` query param: `error_ids` is extracted via `process_raw_response(snuba_response, fields=request.query_params.getlist('field'))` (project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:~84-89), so if the caller doesn't include `error_ids` in `field`, error context silently vanishes with no error; the endpoint should explicitly request the one field it depends on instead of forwarding arbitrary client field selection

Raw epoch float rendered into the LLM prompt: `generate_error_log_message` (project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py) injects e.g. 'at 1737000000.123' via `f'... at {timestamp}'` into the Seer prompt, which is meaningless to the model and to prompt auditors; should be formatted as ISO-8601/human-readable

Duplicated, truthiness-based age/timestamp cross-field validation in src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:~52-60: mutual exclusion is implemented twice in mirrored validators using `if self.initial_data.get('age')`, so `age=0`/`timestamp=0` slip past both checks and a report with neither field validates even though both docstrings claim presence is enforced; should be a single cross-field `validate()` using key-presence checks plus an explicit decision on whether one of the two is required

`timestamp` typed as `IntegerField` in browser_reporting_collector.py:~49 but the W3C working draft defines it as `DOMHighResTimeStamp` (a double); fractional timestamps either 422 (dropping the whole batch since validation is all-or-nothing) or get truncated depending on DRF behavior — `FloatField` is likely correct and should be verified against real payloads

Owner-resolution logic duplicated between `update()` and `create()` in src/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/validators/base/detector.py:~65-79 vs ~119-131 with subtly divergent semantics: `update()` explicitly clears the opposite column and silently no-ops for an actor that is neither user nor team, while `create()` defaults both to None; a single resolver should be extracted so the paths can't drift

Same autofix automation default hardcoded in two files — src/sentry/constants.py:724 and src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py:205 — proven drift-prone by this very PR requiring a lockstep change from 'low' to 'off'; defaults.py should reference `DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT` rather than a string literal

Likely dead code left behind after regex-experiment removal in src/sentry/grouping/parameterization.py: `_handle_regex_match` (~line 340, its only caller was the deleted else-branch), `ParameterizationRegex` (~180-205, only subclass deleted but still exported in `__all__`), and the now single-member alias `ParameterizationExperiment = ParameterizationCallableExperiment` (~268) — verify and remove the leftovers

PR scope: ~a dozen unrelated subsystems (replays, GitHub/GitLab PR comments, browser reporting, grouping experiments, migration no-ops, preprod analytics, workflow engine, frontend Flex migration, devservices config) mixed into one diff, making it unreviewable and bisect-hostile; needs splitting if not a merge-base artifact

Merged-PR comment generation calls `_truncate_title`, `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template`, and `get_environment_info` via `PRCommentWorkflow`/`self` in `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow`/`GitlabPRCommentWorkflow`, but these methods are defined on `CommitContextIntegration`, which the workflow composes rather than inherits, causing AttributeError at runtime and silently breaking all merged-PR suspect comments for GitHub and GitLab integrations.

In `project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, `fetch_error_details` reads unnormalized ISO-8601 string timestamps from raw nodestore event data and mixes them with numeric epoch breadcrumb timestamps, causing TypeError in `error_events.sort(key=lambda x: x["timestamp"])` and `str < float` comparisons, resulting in 500 errors whenever error fetching is enabled (the default) or garbage interleaving of errors into the breadcrumb log sent to Seer.

In `project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, `zip(error_ids, events.values())` positionally pairs error IDs with nodestore `get_multi` results, but the returned dict is keyed by node id with no guarantee of input ordering or None-filling for missing ids, silently misattributing error titles/messages/timestamps to the wrong error IDs.

Detector `owner` field uses `ActorField`, which deserializes `{actor_type, actor_id}` into an `Actor` without verifying the actor exists or belongs to the detector's organization/project and has no `validate_owner`, allowing clients to store nonexistent or cross-org actors as detector owners.
In detector `update`, if the resolved actor is neither `is_user` nor `is_team`, both branches are skipped and the owner silently stays unchanged with no error — a silent no-op on invalid input.

In `organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py`, `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` fires before the `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble")` gate and before any request validation, counting gated-out users and invalid/failed requests as assemble events and inflating the funnel metric.

In `browser_reporting_collector.py`, the validation loop returns 422 on the first invalid report, discarding all valid reports in the same POST batch, so a single attacker-influenceable poison report permanently zeroes out valid metrics in every batch it rides in.

In `browser_reporting_collector.py`, `validate_timestamp`/`validate_age` only enforce mutual exclusion — a report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` passes validation despite the docstrings claiming presence is being validated, accepting spec-invalid reports.

Already-shipped migrations 0917/0920 are rewritten in place as no-op stubs, but environments that ran them as head (dev/self-hosted/staging) have them recorded as applied, risking migration checksum/drift tooling failures and making correctness depend entirely on 0921 being idempotent against already-converted rows.

If nodestore returns a non-numeric timestamp (e.g., an ISO-8601 string), this would raise `TypeError` at runtime. The diff doesn’t prove nodestore timestamps are strings, but it does introduce an unguarded cross-type comparison risk that should be addressed (cast/parse to float or skip invalid timestamps).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `owner = ActorField(required=False, allow_null=True)` and then simply copies the resolved actor into `owner_user_id`/`owner_team_id` in `update()`/`create()`, but the PR also adds explicit tests asserting cross-org owners are rejected (e.g. `test_owner_not_in_organization` in `tests/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/test_organization_detector_index.py` expects a 400 when passing a user from another org). That strongly indicates organization-membership validation exists in the serialization/field resolution layer (likely `ActorField`) even though it’s not rechecked in `update()`/`create()`. The finding’s claim that there is “no organization-membership validation” is therefore not supported by what’s shown in the diff.

Timestamp unit mismatch in `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`: error-event timestamps from nodestore are seconds since epoch (~1.7e9) while RRWeb segment/breadcrumb events carry millisecond timestamps (~1.7e12), so the interleaving comparison always emits all error messages before all breadcrumb messages, defeating the chronological merge and degrading the Seer summary it feeds.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows new logic that interleaves replay segment events with error events by comparing raw `timestamp` values (`while ... error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`) in `gen_request_data`. Error timestamps are taken directly from nodestore event payloads (`timestamp=data.get("timestamp", 0.0)`), while segment event timestamps come from rrweb segment JSON (`event.get("timestamp", 0)`). The code performs no unit normalization or conversion, so it implicitly assumes both sources share the same timestamp unit/scale. The finding’s specific claim that rrweb timestamps are milliseconds and nodestore timestamps are seconds cannot be verified from the diff alone (tests use small/seconds-like floats), but the underlying review issue—missing explicit normalization/validation between two timestamp sources introduced by this change—is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In the same breadcrumb/error merge comparison, a non-numeric breadcrumb `timestamp` value would raise a TypeError from the `<` comparison, causing a 500 error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` in `fetch_error_details` (src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:~109-125) mispairs error IDs with event data because `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a node_id-keyed mapping with no ordering guarantee and omits missing keys entirely; the `if data is not None` guard only helps on backends that return None for misses, making the code backend-dependent — should build a node_id to event_id map and iterate `events.items()`

adjudication.rationale: In `fetch_error_details`, the code builds `node_ids = [Event.generate_node_id(project_id, event_id=id) for id in error_ids]` then calls `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`, and finally zips `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. Because `get_multi` returns a mapping keyed by node_id, it may omit missing keys; if any earlier `error_id` is missing, `events.values()` will be shorter and `zip` will pair subsequent returned event payloads with the wrong `error_id` (e.g., first missing causes all following to shift). The `if data is not None` filter does not prevent mispairing when missing keys are omitted rather than returned as `None`. This is a correctness bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Broad `except Exception: capture_exception(e); return []` in `fetch_error_details` (project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:~121-124) swallows everything including programming errors and silently produces a summary with no error context; the exception should be narrowed or logged at warning with context

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `fetch_error_details()` in `project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py` with a broad `except Exception as e:` that does `sentry_sdk.capture_exception(e)` and then returns an empty list. This can indeed mask unexpected failures (including programming errors) and causes the request to proceed without error context. However, it’s an intentional fallback behavior and not a clearly verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone (it also isn’t fully “silent” since it captures the exception). The review point is still specific and actionable (narrow exception types and/or add logging with replay/project context).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Endpoint's core input depends on the client's `field` query param: `error_ids` is extracted via `process_raw_response(snuba_response, fields=request.query_params.getlist('field'))` (project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:~84-89), so if the caller doesn't include `error_ids` in `field`, error context silently vanishes with no error; the endpoint should explicitly request the one field it depends on instead of forwarding arbitrary client field selection

adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, the code derives `error_ids` from `response = process_raw_response(snuba_response, fields=request.query_params.getlist("field"))` and then `error_ids = response[0].get("error_ids", [])`. This makes the endpoint’s internal ability to fetch error context contingent on the client including `error_ids` in the `field` query param; if `field` excludes it, `error_ids` will be absent and error context will silently be skipped (even when `enable_error_context` is true). The endpoint should request `error_ids` explicitly for its own logic rather than forwarding arbitrary client-selected fields for this internal dependency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw epoch float rendered into the LLM prompt: `generate_error_log_message` (project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py) injects e.g. 'at 1737000000.123' via `f'... at {timestamp}'` into the Seer prompt, which is meaningless to the model and to prompt auditors; should be formatted as ISO-8601/human-readable

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, `generate_error_log_message()` interpolates `timestamp = error["timestamp"]` directly into the prompt via `return f"... at {timestamp}"`, where `timestamp` is a float (see `ErrorEvent` TypedDict and `fetch_error_details()` which sets `timestamp=data.get("timestamp", 0.0)`). This is indeed a raw epoch-style float (the test constructs timestamps via `now.timestamp()`), which is likely not meaningful to the LLM/prompt auditors. adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated, truthiness-based age/timestamp cross-field validation in src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:~52-60: mutual exclusion is implemented twice in mirrored validators using `if self.initial_data.get('age')`, so `age=0`/`timestamp=0` slip past both checks and a report with neither field validates even though both docstrings claim presence is enforced; should be a single cross-field `validate()` using key-presence checks plus an explicit decision on whether one of the two is required

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer` the mutual-exclusion checks are implemented in two mirrored field validators (`validate_timestamp` / `validate_age`) using truthiness (`self.initial_data.get("age")` / `get("timestamp")`). This means key-present-but-falsy values like `age=0` or `timestamp=0` will not trigger the exclusion error, so a payload containing both fields can incorrectly validate. Also, since both fields are `required=False`, a report with neither field will validate (field-level validators won’t run when missing), despite the validators’ docstrings implying presence requirements. This behavior is visible in the diff and is not covered by the added tests (they only test `age=1` with `timestamp`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `timestamp` typed as `IntegerField` in browser_reporting_collector.py:~49 but the W3C working draft defines it as `DOMHighResTimeStamp` (a double); fractional timestamps either 422 (dropping the whole batch since validation is all-or-nothing) or get truncated depending on DRF behavior — `FloatField` is likely correct and should be verified against real payloads

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer` (browser_reporting_collector.py), `timestamp` is validated with `serializers.IntegerField(required=False, min_value=0)`. If real browser payloads send fractional timestamps, this serializer will treat them as invalid (or coerce/truncate depending on DRF internals), and the endpoint will return 422 and reject the entire batch because it exits on the first invalid report (`return Response(..., status=422)`). The diff itself doesn’t confirm that fractional timestamps occur in practice, but the strict integer typing does create a potential standards/compatibility edge case worth verifying.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Owner-resolution logic duplicated between `update()` and `create()` in src/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/validators/base/detector.py:~65-79 vs ~119-131 with subtly divergent semantics: `update()` explicitly clears the opposite column and silently no-ops for an actor that is neither user nor team, while `create()` defaults both to None; a single resolver should be extracted so the paths can't drift

adjudication_records.issue_text: Merged-PR comment generation calls `_truncate_title`, `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template`, and `get_environment_info` via `PRCommentWorkflow`/`self` in `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow`/`GitlabPRCommentWorkflow`, but these methods are defined on `CommitContextIntegration`, which the workflow composes rather than inherits, causing AttributeError at runtime and silently breaking all merged-PR suspect comments for GitHub and GitLab integrations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In `project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, `fetch_error_details` reads unnormalized ISO-8601 string timestamps from raw nodestore event data and mixes them with numeric epoch breadcrumb timestamps, causing TypeError in `error_events.sort(key=lambda x: x["timestamp"])` and `str < float` comparisons, resulting in 500 errors whenever error fetching is enabled (the default) or garbage interleaving of errors into the breadcrumb log sent to Seer.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `fetch_error_details()` and then sorts/compares `ErrorEvent["timestamp"]` numerically (`error_events.sort(key=lambda x: x["timestamp"])` and `error_events[...]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`). But `fetch_error_details()` pulls `timestamp` straight from raw nodestore event payload via `data.get("timestamp", 0.0)` with no normalization/casting. If nodestore returns timestamps as ISO-8601 strings (a plausible/commonly used representation for event payloads), mixing those with breadcrumb `event.get("timestamp")` floats will raise `TypeError` during sorting or comparison. This is a correctness risk introduced by the new error-context interleaving logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In `project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, `zip(error_ids, events.values())` positionally pairs error IDs with nodestore `get_multi` results, but the returned dict is keyed by node id with no guarantee of input ordering or None-filling for missing ids, silently misattributing error titles/messages/timestamps to the wrong error IDs.

adjudication.rationale: In `fetch_error_details` (new in `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`), the code does `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and then builds results with `for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values())`. Since `get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node id, iterating `events.values()` relies on the dict’s iteration order matching the `error_ids`/`node_ids` request order and also assumes missing keys are represented positionally. The diff provides no guarantee of either, so this can misassociate an `event_id` with another event’s payload (or skip/shift on missing entries), producing incorrect titles/messages/timestamps for a given error id.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Detector `owner` field uses `ActorField`, which deserializes `{actor_type, actor_id}` into an `Actor` without verifying the actor exists or belongs to the detector's organization/project and has no `validate_owner`, allowing clients to store nonexistent or cross-org actors as detector owners.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `owner = ActorField(required=False, allow_null=True)` and then persists `owner_user_id`/`owner_team_id` from the deserialized `owner`. However, the PR also adds explicit API tests asserting invalid/cross-org owners are rejected with 400 (`test_invalid_owner`, `test_owner_not_in_organization` in `tests/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/test_organization_detector_index.py`). That indicates the field deserialization/validation path *does* prevent nonexistent or non-member actors, contradicting the finding’s claim that there is “no verification” and clients can store cross-org/nonexistent actors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In detector `update`, if the resolved actor is neither `is_user` nor `is_team`, both branches are skipped and the owner silently stays unchanged with no error — a silent no-op on invalid input.

adjudication.rationale: The added `owner` field is validated by `ActorField` (`owner = ActorField(required=False, allow_null=True)`), and the accompanying tests assert invalid owner strings or owners not in the org return 400 (`test_invalid_owner`, `test_owner_not_in_organization`). adjudication_records.issue_text: In `organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py`, `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` fires before the `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble")` gate and before any request validation, counting gated-out users and invalid/failed requests as assemble events and inflating the funnel metric.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` call at the start of `post()` in `src/sentry/preprod/api/endpoints/organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py`, before the subsequent feature gate `if not features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble", ...)`. As written, requests from users/orgs without the feature (and any request that later fails) will still emit the analytics event, inflating the metric. adjudication_records.issue_text: In `browser_reporting_collector.py`, the validation loop returns 422 on the first invalid report, discarding all valid reports in the same POST batch, so a single attacker-influenceable poison report permanently zeroes out valid metrics in every batch it rides in.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint.post` validating each report and immediately `return Response(..., status=HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY)` on the first invalid item, so any valid reports in the same `raw_data` batch are not processed and their metrics are not incremented (the second processing loop is never reached). However, the finding’s “attacker-influenceable … permanently zeroes out valid metrics in every batch it rides in” framing is overstated: an attacker can only cause their own request to fail, and rejecting an entire batch on any invalid item may be an intentional all-or-nothing validation choice rather than a clear defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In `browser_reporting_collector.py`, `validate_timestamp`/`validate_age` only enforce mutual exclusion — a report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` passes validation despite the docstrings claiming presence is being validated, accepting spec-invalid reports.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer`, both `age` and `timestamp` are declared `required=False`. The per-field validators `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` only run when their respective field is present, and they only reject the *other* field being present via `self.initial_data.get(...)`. Therefore a payload with neither `age` nor `timestamp` will pass `serializer.is_valid()` with no error, despite the comments/docstrings indicating support for two specs where one of these fields should be provided (and the docstrings explicitly talk about presence). This means spec-invalid reports can be accepted by the endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Already-shipped migrations 0917/0920 are rewritten in place as no-op stubs, but environments that ran them as head (dev/self-hosted/staging) have them recorded as applied, risking migration checksum/drift tooling failures and making correctness depend entirely on 0921 being idempotent against already-converted rows.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly rewrites existing migration files 0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py and 0920_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_revised.py to be unconditional no-op stubs (`return`) with comments saying they were never run, and it also deletes the test for 0917. Editing already-numbered migrations in place is a concrete, diff-grounded risk: any environment/tooling that expects migration files to be immutable (or that audits migration content) could flag drift, and new installs will now skip the conversion logic in 0917/0920 and depend on a later migration (mentioned as 0921, not shown) to perform/cover the data move safely. However, the claim that these were “already-shipped” and “recorded as applied” in some environments, and that checksum tooling will definitely fail, is not directly verifiable from the diff alone, so it’s best treated as an important process/robustness concern rather than a proven functional defect.
